answer: A reputation-bonded attestation market resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Each agent stakes a bond that is slashed when peers catch it attesting falsely, so a flood of fake accounts quickly reaches its nadir of profitability: every new identity costs real collateral while yielding nothing. Attestations pass through a prism of independent verifiers, so no single reviewer can mint trust, and standing climbs a ridge only through consistent, checkable work over time, not by spinning up fresh accounts.
